newsitem.title: USA: Cleveland Clinic fined by nuclear agency.
newsitem.headline: Cleveland Clinic fined by nuclear agency.

text.p: A Cleveland hospital that has treated Jordan's King Hussein and Saudi Arabia's royal family will be fined $5,000 for violating regulations related to radioactive materials, a U.S. government spokesman said on Friday.

The Cleveland Clinic Foundation was fined for not having annual retraining of laboratory staff and for not conducting an annual audit of laboratory functions, the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said.
The hospital quickly corrected the violations. "None had a direct impact on patient safety," nor did they involve unnecessary worker exposure to the materials, NRC spokesman Jan Strasma said.

It is the fifth time since 1986 the Cleveland Clinic has been fined by the NRC -- more than any other U.S. medical facility, Strasma said. While the NRC can fine nuclear power plants up to $110,000 a day for violations, Strasma said $2,500 to $5,000 was a typical fine for medical facilities.

Dr. John Clough, Cleveland Clinic director of health affairs, said a quarterly newsletter was substituted for a required annual refresher training course and an annual audit of laboratory functions was scheduled but not completed on time.
"While we acknowledge we didn't follow the letter of the law, we believe ... we followed the spirit of it," Clough said. "We will follow the letter of the law from now on."

The Clinic, whose specialities include open-heart surgery and organ transplants, is licensed to have cobalt-60, iodine radioisotopes and other radioactive materials for treatment of some cancer and other illnesses and for research, Clough said.
